clue.text: Preserving material to create a short piece of poetry

parts.note: to form something is to create it

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a line is a single piece of a poem

explanation.surface: Someone looks for something to preserve a brief poem with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. LINE loses its last letter to become LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin is a solution of formaldehyde used to preserve biological specimens.

clue.text: Quick wit aboard English vessel

parts.note: on means aboard, as in on a ship
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A clever joker is travelling on an English ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short witty remark, a single quick joke.

clue.text: Part of pop song about western fighter

indicators.note: about means the middle-eight phrase goes around the letter for western

parts.note: the middle eight is the contrasting section in the middle of a pop song

explanation.surface: A section of a pop song about a cowboy hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle eight is an eight-bar bridge in a song; W goes into it after MIDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a boxer in the weight class between welterweight and light heavyweight.

clue.text: Educational material not being broadcast as much

indicators.note: as much closes the phrase opened by not, so the less piece wraps the broadcast piece in the clue but comes first

parts.note: with 'as much' at the end of the clue, 'not ... as much' means less
a programme being broadcast is on

explanation.surface: Schools material is being aired on television less often.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'not ... as much' is split by 'being broadcast', so its piece comes first in the answer even though its words surround the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, or a passage set for study.

clue.text: Among inhumane Romans, the most brutal of tyrants

indicators.note: among says the answer sits within the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A claim that, of the cruel Romans, one emperor was the worst tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero, the Roman emperor, is remembered as a byword for tyranny and cruelty.

clue.text: Look like holidaymakers in location on ocean, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: a site is a location and the sea is the ocean, so a site on the sea gives SITE SEA

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers looking around a spot by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SITE SEA spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to look round the famous sights, as tourists on holiday do.

clue.text: This Orientals fed upon, originally

indicators.note: originally means take the first, original letter of each word

explanation.surface: Pointing at a food eaten by people in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the initials spell the answer, and the clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, bean curd, is a staple food across East Asia.

clue.text: Explanatory text a writer finally got into magazine

indicators.note: got into means the letters are placed inside the magazine word

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of writer

explanation.surface: A writer at last gets an explanatory piece published in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: A glossy is a magazine on shiny paper; A plus the final R of writer slip in before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms with explanations, usually at the back of a book.

clue.text: Way-out questions about voting oddly exploit Labour leader

indicators.note: oddly means the letters are arranged in an odd, new order
leader means the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Strange questions about how people vote could benefit the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' looks like slang for crazy, but it belongs to the definition: these questions are put to voters on their way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll surveys voters as they leave the polling station, asking how they voted.

clue.text: Cape is what's over your shoulders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a headland jutting into the sea
second meaning: the part of the body on top of the shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: A cape is also a garment over the shoulders, which makes the clue read as one idea; the two senses are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a promontory, as in Beachy Head, and also the part of the body sitting above the neck.

clue.text: Girl's payments, of a kind, covering old-time musical entertainment

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's is the girl's

indicators.note: covering means the payment word wraps around the old-time letters

parts.note: cheques are one kind of payment
OT stands for old time, as in overtime abbreviations; here old-time gives OT

explanation.surface: A girl's fees cover some old-fashioned music shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is a short form of Diana; 'of a kind' tells you cheques are just one form of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Discotheques are nightclubs where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Doubt in long search covering one in position to run

indicators.note: covering means the search word sits on top of the letter for one in this down answer

parts.note: a quest is a long search
I is the Roman numeral for one
on (your) mark is where a runner is set at the start of a race

explanation.surface: Uncertainty during a lengthy search over someone's position before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' after Doubt is a link word. 'On your marks' is the call to runners at the start line.
explanation.definitionFit: A question mark is a point of doubt or uncertainty, as in 'there is a question mark over his future'.

clue.text: Dreadful fires — no end of destruction to be contained

definitions.text: Dreadful fires — no end of destruction to be contained

indicators.note: dreadful means the following letters are in a terrible mess, rearranged
end of means the last letter of destruction

explanation.surface: Terrible blazes cause destruction without end and must be brought under control.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRES, NO and N are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernos are huge, raging fires that need to be brought under control.

clue.text: Small complaint, commonly, resulting in rebuke

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cold is a common complaint, an ailment

explanation.surface: A small grumble ends up as a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to reprimand them angrily.

clue.text: Bones found in chest in ship's rear area

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Bones from a chest discovered at the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' before ship's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Large plant removed from middle of road when it's cut

indicators.note: middle of means keep only the central letters of the road word
when it's cut says the road word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a street is a road

explanation.surface: A tree is taken away from the middle of a road after it is felled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a tall woody perennial, the largest kind of plant.

clue.text: Set-up receiving, unusually, live European broadcast

indicators.note: receiving means the upward set word takes the other letters inside it
up in a down answer means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of live appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A set-up taking in live European material to put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' reads as an arrangement, but 'up' is the reversal signal working on 'Set' in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To televise is to broadcast on television.

clue.text: Turn out to demonstrate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turn out to be
second meaning: show something to be true

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Prove means both to turn out to be (prove useful) and to establish as true by evidence.

clue.text: Artist exhibited in opening Italian work of art

indicators.note: exhibited in means the artist is shown inside the other letters

parts.note: a port is an opening, such as a porthole or gunport
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's work shown at an opening of Italian art.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or picture of a person, an artwork.

clue.text: Hear about old person with right philosophy?

indicators.note: about means the hearing word goes around the letter for old

parts.note: a court hears, or tries, a case

explanation.surface: Listening to stories of an elderly person with sound views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like it signals a sound-alike, but it is the legal sense: to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a Conservative, holding right-wing politics; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Find another position for idiot breaking rule

indicators.note: breaking means the idiot word bursts into the middle of the rule word

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Moving a fool to a new job because he broke the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign someone is to transfer them to a different job or post.

clue.text: Drink passed around a camp on the veldt

indicators.note: passed around means the drink word goes around the letter a

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer

explanation.surface: A drink is handed round a campsite in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is an encampment protected by a circle of wagons, a South African term; the veldt is South African grassland.

clue.text: I would back ally so flaky? Not true

indicators.note: back means the short form of I would is read in reverse

parts.note: I'd, written without the apostrophe, is short for I would

indicators.note: flaky means the letters of ally so crumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wondering if they would turn their back on such an unreliable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Disloyal means unfaithful, not staying true to a person or cause.

clue.text: Italian food I'm regrettably passing up

indicators.note: passing up in a down answer means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: I'm without the apostrophe
alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: A diner sadly declining an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing up' reads as turning down the food; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spiced, cured sausage originating from Italy.

clue.text: Fruit in state exactly as reported

parts.note: Victoria is a state of Australia

indicators.note: as reported means the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: plumb means exactly, as in plumb in the middle

explanation.surface: Fruit being in a particular condition, just as described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'state' is the Australian state, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria plum is a popular English variety of plum, a sweet stone fruit.

clue.text: In certain states, minimal change in concentration

indicators.note: in here means the answer is found inside the next word

explanation.surface: Little alteration in levels of focus for some conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain states' are countries such as the United States, where the smallest coin is the cent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, the smallest coin of small change in the US.

clue.text: Member of family I released from a group of soldiers

indicators.note: released from means the letter I is let go out of the soldiers' word

parts.note: a unit is a group of soldiers

explanation.surface: A relative being discharged from an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' in the clue is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a relative, the sister of one's parent.

clue.text: Opposed to something it is added to

parts.note: something, in the sense of a single thing, gives the article a
gin and it is a cocktail of gin with Italian vermouth, so gin is what it is added to

explanation.surface: Against something that something else is added to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Contains changes? Okay

indicators.note: changes means the letters of contains are altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether an approved document includes amendments.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official approval, to say okay.

clue.text: Fine man on board performing brain operations

parts.note: fine means thin, as in a fine thread
the king is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A good chess player at work using his brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brain operations' suggests surgery but just means thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking is using the mind, the brain's activity of reasoning.
